Se ordena a la población de menos a más: The population is sorted from lowest to highest income and, for each cumulative fraction of the population $p$, the fraction of income it holds, $q$, is plotted. If everyone earned the same, 20 % of people would have 20 % of income and the curve would be the diagonal; the further it departs from it downward, the more unequal the distribution.
Es el doble del área entre la diagonal y: It is twice the area between the diagonal and the curve: 0 if everyone has the same and almost 1 if a single person has everything. With the points of the curve it is computed by trapezoids, $G = 1 − Σ (p_i − p_{i−1})(q_i + q_{i−1})$. Many textbooks use $I_G = {Σ (p_i − q_i)}/{Σ p_i}$, which gives almost the same when there are many groups. Spain is around 0.32; the Nordic countries, close to 0.25; South Africa, above 0.6.
Divide la renta del 20 % más rico entre: It divides the income of the richest 20 % by that of the poorest 20 %. It is the other inequality measure published by the INE (Spain's national statistics institute) and Eurostat, and it is understood without formulas: a 5 means the richest fifth has five times the income of the poorest.
